narration: Somewhere in this night sky is the brightest black hole we know of. From here you cannot see it at all.
Bring it to the edge of our galaxy and it becomes the brightest star in the night, brighter than Venus.
At a thousand light-years the night turns blue. The sky is lit by something you still see as a point.
At this distance it shines exactly as bright as our own Sun.
Closer still, and the forest on the slopes begins to burn.
And at a tenth of a light-year the disc fills the sky. Its horizon alone is eight hundred times the distance from the Earth to the Sun.
